text: Draw context level, 1* level and 2™ level Data Flow Diagrams for the below case study Case study - Archie’s online store Archie’s is store which deal with gift items. It has an online store. Order Processing System (OPS) is an important part of an online store. The online store has the following subsystems: an online product catalog for user browsing, the order processing system for user orders, the financial department, which contacts credit card companies for financial charges and the shipping department, which is responsible for packaging products and shipping. Online order processing must interact with other components and provide the following service to customers: First of all the customer has to log in into the system. If customer is not a member then he cari only view the products but can not place order for it. To place an order customer has to make registration. Each registered customer has an online shopping cart, which allows him to add and remove items to be purchased. A registered customer is able to check out using a credit card. A transaction is approved only when the financial department has verified the credit card. Before the transaction is completed, a registered customer should be able to learn about his order’s estimated arrival date, which is determined by the order processing time of i the shipping department. A registered customer can choose to cancel the transaction by clearing all items in the shopping cart. Archie’s online store must be available as a web accessible system. Customers can use popular internet browsers to interact with Archie’s online store.
